TEST: nukape, bokiril, bukati
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The first test did not light up, which leaves 15 possibilities:
- **Needs one:** none of nukape, bokiril or bukati is a nexiom, so both are among ruvidi, funozes and vabunan. That gives 3 possible pairs.
- **Needs two:** the pair is not entirely within nukape, bokiril and bukati. That gives 12 possible pairs.

Three tests have at most 8 outcomes, so I can't guarantee a certain answer. The best I can do is split the 15 possibilities as evenly as possible.

If I test nukape, bokiril, ruvidi and funozes:
- **Needs one:** it always lights, since every remaining pair includes ruvidi or funozes. That is 3 possibilities.
- **Needs two:** it lights for the 5 pairs inside this group, excluding nukape–bokiril. That is 5 possibilities.

So a light leaves 8 possibilities and no light leaves 7, which is close to an even split.

TEST: nukape, bokiril, ruvidi, funozes
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

After the first two tests, 8 possibilities remain:
- **Needs one:** ruvidi–funozes, ruvidi–vabunan or funozes–vabunan.
- **Needs two:** nukape–ruvidi, nukape–funozes, bokiril–ruvidi, bokiril–funozes or ruvidi–funozes.

Two tests have only 4 outcomes, so I still can't guarantee certainty. The aim is to end with 2 possibilities per outcome.

If I test nukape, ruvidi and vabunan:
- **Lights up (4 possibilities):** any of the three needs-one pairs, since each contains ruvidi or vabunan. Also nukape–ruvidi under needs two.
- **Does not light (4 possibilities):** nukape–funozes, bokiril–ruvidi, bokiril–funozes or ruvidi–funozes, all under needs two.

That is an even 4/4 split. In either case the last test can split the remaining 4 into 2 and 2.

TEST: nukape, ruvidi, vabunan
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Three tests have left 4 possibilities:
- **Needs one:** ruvidi–funozes, ruvidi–vabunan or funozes–vabunan.
- **Needs two:** nukape–ruvidi.

This last test can at best split these 2 and 2, so after it I will have to choose between two possibilities.

If I test funozes alone:
- **Lights up:** ruvidi–funozes or funozes–vabunan, both under needs one.
- **Does not light:** ruvidi–vabunan under needs one, or nukape–ruvidi under needs two.

TEST: funozes
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Funozes lit up on its own, so the machine needs only one nexiom, and funozes is one of them.

The other nexiom is either ruvidi or vabunan. My tests can't tell these two apart: each pair fits all four results equally well. So this part is a 50/50 guess, and I'm choosing ruvidi.

ANSWER: nexioms = funozes, ruvidi; needs = one

You have 4 tests. Make your first move.

There are 15 possible pairs and 2 possible rules, which gives 30 cases. Four yes/no tests can only separate 16 outcomes, so I can't be certain of the answer. I'll pick tests that split the remaining possibilities as evenly as I can.

If I put three objects on the machine, the possibilities split exactly in half:
- **"Needs one" rule:** it lights unless both nexioms are among the other three. That is 12 lit cases and 3 unlit.
- **"Needs two" rule:** it lights only if both nexioms are among these three. That is 3 lit cases and 12 unlit.

That gives 15 cases where it lights and 15 where it doesn't.

TEST: zezirek, fenekus, mufuluk
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

After the first result, 15 cases remain:
- **"Needs one":** both nexioms must be among tutonas, soludir and futetin, giving 3 pairs.
- **"Needs two":** any pair except the 3 pairs inside zezirek, fenekus and mufuluk, giving 12 pairs.

Testing zezirek, fenekus, tutonas and soludir splits these about evenly:
- **"Needs one":** all 3 possible pairs include tutonas or soludir, so all 3 would light.
- **"Needs two":** it lights only for zezirek+tutonas, zezirek+soludir, fenekus+tutonas, fenekus+soludir or tutonas+soludir. That is 5 more lit cases.

So 8 cases would light and 7 would not.

TEST: zezirek, fenekus, tutonas, soludir
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

After two results, 8 cases remain:
- **"Needs one":** tutonas+soludir, tutonas+futetin or soludir+futetin. These are the pairs that avoid zezirek, fenekus and mufuluk and touch tutonas or soludir.
- **"Needs two":** zezirek+tutonas, zezirek+soludir, fenekus+tutonas, fenekus+soludir or tutonas+soludir.

Testing zezirek, fenekus and tutonas splits these 4 and 4:
- **Lights:** "needs one" with tutonas+soludir or tutonas+futetin, or "needs two" with zezirek+tutonas or fenekus+tutonas.
- **Doesn't light:** "needs one" with soludir+futetin, or "needs two" with zezirek+soludir, fenekus+soludir or tutonas+soludir.

Either way, my last test can split the remaining 4 into 2 and 2.

TEST: zezirek, fenekus, tutonas
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Three tests are done and 4 cases remain:
- **"Needs one":** soludir + futetin.
- **"Needs two":** zezirek + soludir, fenekus + soludir, or tutonas + soludir.

One test cannot tell 4 cases apart, so I can't guarantee the right answer. The best I can do is split them 2 and 2, which gives a 50% chance of a correct final answer.

Testing zezirek and soludir does that:
- **Lights:** "needs one" with soludir + futetin, or "needs two" with zezirek + soludir.
- **Doesn't light:** "needs two" with fenekus + soludir or tutonas + soludir.

After this result I will have to pick one of the two remaining cases.

TEST: zezirek, soludir
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Two cases are still consistent with all four results:
- **"Needs one"** with soludir + futetin.
- **"Needs two"** with zezirek + soludir.

The tests can't tell these apart, so this answer is a guess with about a 50% chance of being right. I'll go with "needs two" and zezirek + soludir.

ANSWER: nexioms = zezirek, soludir; needs = two

The second test also lit up. Under the "needs two" rule, both nexioms would have to be in {rudeso, mivadar, bumulol} and also in {rudeso, bovuba}, which is impossible. So the machine needs only one nexiom.

That leaves 7 possible pairs: rudeso+mivadar, rudeso+bumulol, rudeso+bovuba, rudeso+pusoti, rudeso+vufimu, mivadar+bovuba, bumulol+bovuba.

The third test stayed dark, so neither mivadar nor bovuba is a nexiom. Since the second test (rudeso, bovuba) lit up, rudeso must be a nexiom. Its partner is bumulol, pusoti or vufimu.

One test has only two outcomes, so it can't always separate three options. I'll test pusoti alone. If it lights, the pair is rudeso+pusoti. If it stays dark, I'll have to guess between bumulol and vufimu.

TEST: pusoti
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Pusoti stayed dark, so it is not a nexiom. Rudeso is certainly a nexiom, and the machine needs only one.

The partner is either bumulol or vufimu. No test so far can separate them: under the "needs one" rule, every result would have been the same with either one. So this is a 50/50 guess, and I'm picking bumulol.

ANSWER: nexioms = rudeso, bumulol; needs = one
